issues.legal_issue: A thekedar acquires hereditary-tenant status when the land was in the thekedar’s personal cultivation on the specified date and the theka was granted for personal cultivation by the thekedar.
material_facts: The plaintiffs were thekedars of the disputed land and were in possession of and personally cultivating it on 1 May 1950.
The theka was created for the thekedars’ personal cultivation of the land, rather than as consideration for other duties such as collecting rent from other tenants.
The thekedars had been personally cultivating the land for about eleven years and had been ejected from it.
issues.conclusion: The thekedars acquired hereditary-tenant status and, having been ejected, were entitled to regain possession.
issues.legal_principle: Section 12(1) of the U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, 1950 deems a thekedar to be a hereditary tenant where the land was in the thekedar’s personal cultivation on 1 May 1950 and the theka was made with a view to the thekedar’s personal cultivation; an ejected hereditary tenant may regain possession. Section 12(2) permits evidence of personal cultivation since the commencement of the theka to show that it was of that nature. A thekedar appointed to collect rent who is merely allowed incidentally to cultivate the lessor’s land is instead an asami under section 13(2). The Court applied Babu Noorul Hasan Khan v. Ram Prasad Singh and Raghunandan Singh v. Brij Mohan Singh.

rule.if: thekedar_claim_to_recover_land and personal_cultivation_on_qualifying_date and theka_granted_for_personal_cultivation and thekedar_was_ejected

predicates.thekedar_claim_to_recover_land: A person claiming as a thekedar sought to recover land on the basis of the theka.
predicates.personal_cultivation_on_qualifying_date: The land was in the thekedar’s personal cultivation on the legally relevant date.
predicates.theka_granted_for_personal_cultivation: The theka was granted for the thekedar’s personal cultivation of the land, rather than as an incident of other duties.
predicates.thekedar_was_ejected: The thekedar was ejected from the land after the qualifying date.

issues.definition: When a thekedar seeking to recover land personally cultivated it on the qualifying date under a theka granted for that purpose and was later ejected, the thekedar is entitled to recover it as a hereditary tenant.

issues.legal_issue: A person cannot acquire adhivasi status on the basis of cultivatory possession when that possession is unlawful.
material_facts: The lessees claimed that they were in cultivatory possession during 1359 Fasli and had thereby acquired adhivasi rights.
The thekedars had acquired hereditary-tenant status and were entitled to the land; the zamindars therefore had no right to induct the lessees after depriving the thekedars of possession.
The lessees’ possession during 1359 Fasli was consequently unlawful against the thekedars.
issues.conclusion: The lessees did not acquire adhivasi rights and the hereditary tenants were entitled to a decree for possession.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3 of the U.P. Land Reforms (Supplementary) Act, 1952 confers adhivasi status on a qualifying person in cultivatory possession during 1359 Fasli, subject to the section’s conditions. Cultivatory possession for this purpose must be lawful; a person who enters or remains on land without a lawful right cannot acquire the status merely through such possession. The Court relied on Sonawati v. Sri Ram.

predicates.adhivasi_status_claim_under_supplementar: A person claimed land status on the basis of cultivatory possession under a supplementary land-reform scheme.
predicates.cultivatory_possession_during_relevant_y: The claimant was in cultivatory possession of the land during the legally relevant year.
predicates.possession_unlawful: The claimant had no lawful right to possess the land, including because another person had the superior right to it and the claimant was inducted without authority.

issues.definition: A claimant who seeks adhivasi status based on cultivatory possession during the relevant year does not acquire that status if the possession was unlawful.
